boards.title: Your First Weekend at Rhode Island School of Design, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented through RISD’s documented campus spaces, collections and student exhibitions.

cards.title: Start with a campus-landmark pause
cards.subtitle: RISD Beach · Benefit Street
cards.notes: Begin by locating the lawn between Waterman and Angell streets; use it as a simple outdoor checkpoint before exploring nearby buildings.
cards.short_summary: A named campus lawn for an easy first orientation stop.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD identifies RISD Beach as the grass on Benefit Street between Waterman and Angell streets.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus location; follow posted campus guidance.

cards.title: Get the campus layout in hand
cards.subtitle: RISD campus · Providence
cards.notes: Open the official map before choosing a route. It labels buildings, outdoor spaces, dining sites, galleries and key services across campus.
cards.short_summary: An official map anchors the rest of the weekend route.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD directs visitors to its online campus map for specific buildings and offices.
cards.access_notes: Available online; use the current map before traveling between sites.

cards.title: Browse the art-and-design stacks
cards.subtitle: Roger Mandle Building · 15 Westminster Street
cards.notes: Set aside time to see the circulating collection, artists’ books and Materials Resource Center; confirm entry and borrowing rules at the desk.
cards.short_summary: A documented campus library with extensive art and design resources.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says Fleet Library has a circulating collection of more than 150,000 books and includes a Materials Resource Center and artists’ books.
cards.access_notes: Check current library access and service hours before visiting.

cards.title: Look closely at the Nature Lab
cards.subtitle: Waterman Building · 13 Waterman Street
cards.notes: Visit with a specific visual question in mind, then ask staff about current access to the preserved-specimen collection and microscopy resources.
cards.short_summary: A RISD resource linking art, design and natural science.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD describes the Nature Lab as holding more than 80,000 preserved natural-science specimens plus microscopy and micro-imaging systems.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current hours and access procedures with the Nature Lab.

cards.title: Make time for the museum collection
cards.subtitle: 20 North Main Street / 224 Benefit Street
cards.notes: Choose a gallery or two rather than rushing the whole museum. Bring your RISD ID and check the museum’s current visitor information first.
cards.short_summary: A museum stop with free admission for RISD students carrying valid ID.
cards.evidence_claim: The RISD Museum states that RISD students receive free admission with valid college ID.
cards.access_notes: Current hours list Tue–Sun service; review closures and ticket guidance before arrival.

cards.title: See a current student exhibition
cards.subtitle: Chace Center, 2nd floor · 20 North Main Street
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition dates, then spend time with the show’s labels and installation. The gallery is a direct view of student-curated work.
cards.short_summary: A public-facing RISD gallery for student work and curatorial projects.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says the Gelman Student Exhibitions Gallery is accessible to museum visitors and the general public and offers student exhibition experience.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists Tues–Sun, 10 am–5 pm; confirm exhibition availability before going.

cards.title: Add Market Square to your bearings
cards.subtitle: Market Square · RISD campus
cards.notes: Use this map-listed campus space as a waypoint while connecting the downtown-facing buildings to the rest of the RISD route.
cards.short_summary: A named key space on RISD’s official campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD’s campus map lists Market Square among its key spaces.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor/shared campus space; observe any event setup or posted restrictions.

cards.title: Take a short outdoor reset
cards.subtitle: Farnum Park · RISD campus
cards.notes: Build in a brief stop at this named outdoor space, then use the campus map to decide whether to continue toward studios or downtown.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed RISD outdoor space for a route break.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD’s campus map directory identifies Farnum Park as an outdoor space.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space; check conditions and posted campus information.

cards.title: Trace another named outdoor space
cards.subtitle: Frazier Terrace · RISD campus
cards.notes: Use Frazier Terrace as a quiet map-reading stop. It helps turn a first walk through campus into a route you can repeat independently.
cards.short_summary: A documented outdoor waypoint on the RISD campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD’s campus map directory identifies Frazier Terrace as an outdoor space.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space; follow campus signage and any temporary restrictions.

cards.title: End near a map-listed patio
cards.subtitle: Metcalf Refectory Patio · RISD campus
cards.notes: Finish your walk by locating this named patio near the Refectory, then review the dining information separately if you plan to purchase food.
cards.short_summary: A named patio that closes the route near a campus dining building.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD’s campus map directory lists the Metcalf Refectory Patio among its outdoor spaces.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor patio location; dining purchases, if any, are separate.
